proposals.before: Judged by these precedents, Yilige's remonstrance was stern and commanding — nearly the bearing of the gentlemen of old.
proposals.after: Judged by these precedents, Yilage's remonstrance was stern and commanding — nearly the bearing of the gentlemen of old.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic misspells the chapter subject Yelage as Yilige.

proposals.before: When the Zhou emperor Shizong returned north ill, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy were.
proposals.after: When the Zhou ruler Rong returned ill, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy were.
proposals.reason: Chinese 周主榮 names the Zhou ruler as Rong; idiomatic invents temple name Shizong and adds north.

decisions.reason: Chinese 夷臘葛 is the chapter subject Yilage (耶律夷臘葛); idiomatic's Yilige is a misspelling, and the proposed Yilage matches the rest of the chapter.

decisions.after: When the Later Zhou emperor Chai Rong returned because of illness, Siwen withdrew to Yijin and pretended not to know where the enemy was.
decisions.reason: 周主榮 identifies the Later Zhou emperor Chai Rong; the source says he returned because of illness but does not say that he returned north.
